properties.title: Forecasting Patient Trajectories from the Electronic Health Records with Action-Conditioned World Models

membership.reason: Implements EHR-WM, an action-conditioned state-dependent linearization latent world model over 6-hour discretized MIMIC-IV trajectories with decoded observation forecasting and matched-initial-state action perturbation.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L2 action-conditioned world model (WT_EHR); Figure 5 MPC perturbation is exploratory action-sensitivity evidence without specified regimens or MPC formulation.

properties.backbone: Feedforward state encoder f_phi (D=128) + state-dependent linearization predictor F_theta(z_t, a_t) + SIGReg + curriculum teacher forcing (4.39M params)

properties.flow: 6h binned EHR (x_t, mask_t, a_t) -> encoder f_phi -> z_t -> second-order linearization rollout z_hat_{t+1} = z_t + F_theta(z_t, a_t) Delta z_t -> linear probes & observation decoder

properties.purpose: Multi-step ICU patient trajectory forecasting, downstream risk prediction, and action-conditioned trajectory exploration.

evidence_fragments.content: Rather than modeling clinical events solely through autoregressive token prediction, our framework explicitly separates patient states from observed clinical actions and learns their evolution through a state- and action-conditioned transition operator. At its core is a state-dependent linearization predictor that propagates local changes in latent patient state, enabling time-resolved prediction, multi-step rollout, and action-conditioned simulation.

We construct longitudinal patient trajectories from MIMIC-IV (31) using the MEDS schema (5, 53) and partition patients into disjoint training, validation, and test cohorts. To prevent information leakage, all preprocessing statistics, including normalization parameters and feature frequencies, are computed on the training split and applied unchanged to validation and test1.
Each variable is then represented by a two-channel encoding consisting of its normalized value and a corresponding binary observation mask to encode missingness.
We therefore employ a curriculum over prediction horizon and input distribution, combining teacher forcing with a sliding-window training scheme (12, 36, 83).

[paraphrase (visual p.10)] Table 1 compares EHR-WM (4.39M params, Rollout and Oracle) against GBM/XGBoost, CLMBR (141M), MOTOR (143M), CoxPH, DeepHit (145k), and DeepSurv (133k) across 10 tasks (e.g., ICU Admission AUC 0.891±0.008 Rollout / 0.894±0.009 Oracle; Sepsis 0.786±0.012 / 0.782±0.013; 30-day Readmission C-Index 0.822±0.011 / 0.816±0.011). Section 4 text on p. 10 summarizes Figure 4 per-variable R2 and MAE across 79 continuous clinical variables over increasing forecast horizons against global mean, LOCF, ridge, GRU-D, Latent ODE, and Transformer baselines.

In Figure 5, we illustrate this behavior for 30-day readmission by comparing trajectories generated under the observed treatment sequence with trajectories generated under an alternative sequence selected using model predictive control (MPC) (29, 35, 56, 69). Both rollouts begin from the same latent patient state, such that differences in the resulting trajectories arise from changes to the action sequence supplied to the transition model.

evidence_fragments.content: Importantly, these intervention-conditioned rollouts should not be interpreted as counterfactual or causal estimates of treatment effects. EHR-WM is trained on observational clinical data and does not identify the causal effect of an intervention from confounded treatment assignment.

[paraphrase (visual p.45)] Figures 22 (p. 45) and 23 (p. 46) report per-feature R2 and MAE for decoded long-horizon rollouts in the 12-24h and 24-48h prediction windows across 79 clinical variables against G.Mean, LOCF, Ridge, GRU-D, L-ODE, and Transformer baselines.
We impose a discrete-time structure by partitioning each patient timeline into fixed intervals of Δ= 6 hours (Experiment in Appendix Section G.3).
Observed medication administrations within each time window are modeled explicitly as a binary clinical action vector 𝑎𝑡∈{ 0, 1}𝑑𝑎.
Let Δ𝑧𝑡 = 𝑧𝑡 − 𝑧𝑡−1. The next state is predicted as ˆ𝑧𝑡+1 = 𝑧𝑡 + 𝐹𝜃(𝑧𝑡, 𝑎𝑡)Δ𝑧𝑡, (3) which propagates the previous latent displacement through a state- and action-dependent linear map.
The full objective is L=L pred+𝜆 sigLSIGReg.(6)

We jointly increase the prediction horizon 𝑘 while annealing 𝜌, transitioning from fully teacher-
forced one-step prediction to partially autoregressive multi-step rollouts.

capability_assessments.rationale: Action-conditioned latent EHR world model with persistent augmented state (z_t, Delta z_t) and learned state-dependent linearization F_theta(z_t, a_t), evaluated on multi-step decoded clinical forecasting across 79 variables (0-48h, Figs. 4, 19-23), 10 downstream tasks (Table 1), and action-conditioning ablation (Fig. 6), supporting L2 (matching legacy_cells.Z). Downgraded from L3 because Figure 5 (p. 11) is an exploratory action-sensitivity plot comparing observed vs unspecified MPC-perturbed trajectories without reporting sample size N, named clinical alternative regimens, or the MPC optimization specification promised for Appendix D.4 (p. 22).

limitations: Restricted to single-center MIMIC-IV ICU cohort and top-k frequent variables.
Multiplicative transition rule z_hat_{t+1} = z_t + F_theta(z_t, a_t) Delta z_t has limited action response when Delta z_t ~ 0.
Observational action-conditioned rollouts do not establish causal treatment effects.

Figure 5 (p. 11) compares observed vs MPC-perturbed 30-day readmission trajectories without reporting sample size N, specific alternative medication sequences, or the MPC objective/horizon setup referenced for Appendix D.4 (p. 22).

legacy_cells.B: Forecasting Patient Trajectories from the Electronic Health Records with Action-Conditioned World Models
legacy_cells.C: Lee, Simon A., Sha, Jiahang Hank, Chung, Soomin, Akamatsu, Kai, Halperin, Eran, Chiang, Jeffrey N.
legacy_cells.O: Acute myocardial infarction, lupus, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, celiac disease, pancreatic cancer, ICU admission, long length of stay, 30-day readmission, and sepsis are among the evaluated outcomes.
legacy_cells.S: Can a learned action-conditioned latent patient trajectory forecast future clinical measurements and preserve downstream predictive information under free-running rollout?
legacy_cells.T: Patients in MIMIC-IV longitudinal EHR trajectories, partitioned into training, validation, and test cohorts.
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: Structured EHR observations including vital signs, laboratory measurements, demographics, normalized values and observation masks, with binary medication-administration actions.
legacy_cells.AJ: Feedforward projection encoder: linear projection, LayerNorm, ReLU, dropout, and linear projection to a 128-dimensional latent state.
legacy_cells.AN: Continuous variables are z-score normalized and represented with value and binary observation-mask channels. Unobserved normalized values are set to zero with mask zero.
legacy_cells.AQ: Temporal-discretization audit compared 3-, 6-, 9-, and 12-hour bins on downstream performance; the paper reports best results at 6 hours.
legacy_cells.AT: No filtering or belief update is described. Each observed x_t is encoded as z_t=f_phi(x_t); free-running forecasts then propagate predicted states.
legacy_cells.BD: Binary medication-administration vector over medication codes. The paper does not specify dose, route, or duration attributes.
legacy_cells.BL: Fixed 6-hour bins; training sequences have length T=16.
legacy_cells.BN: The transition uses a state- and action-dependent local linearization of latent increments. Spectral normalization bounds the learned operator, and SIGReg regularizes latent geometry.
legacy_cells.BP: Forecasts initialize from the first two observed timepoints; training sequences have length 16 at 6-hour resolution.
legacy_cells.BS: Autoregressively generated latent states are decoded by a shared linear decoder into future continuous clinical-variable values.
legacy_cells.BT: Linear probes evaluate binary classification and time-to-event outcomes on latent states; a shared linear decoder predicts continuous clinical measurements.
legacy_cells.BV: Multi-step latent prediction squared-error loss plus SIGReg: L = L_pred + lambda_sig L_SIGReg.
legacy_cells.CA: Training used one Apple MacBook Pro with Apple M4 chip and 48 GB unified memory using MPS; full-model training took roughly 13 hours.
legacy_cells.CD: 24–48 hours for the reported clinical-measurement forecasting windows.
legacy_cells.DZ: Latent trajectory discriminator performance is reported near chance (AUROC approximately 0.5) for generated versus encoder-derived trajectories.
legacy_cells.EB: Holding the initial latent patient state fixed, an alternative action sequence produced a distinct time-resolved readmission-risk trajectory from the observed-treatment sequence. This demonstrates action sensitivity, not causal treatment effect.
legacy_cells.EG: The model has 4.39M parameters versus 141M and 143M for the compared CLMBR and MOTOR models; the authors describe an approximately 30× smaller parameter footprint.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with global mean, LOCF, Ridge Regression, GRU-D, Latent ODE, Transformer, XGBoost, CLMBR, MOTOR, CoxPH, DeepHit, and DeepSurv. EHR-WM is competitive on some outcomes but task-dependent and weaker than specialized baselines on others.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations remove action conditioning, teacher forcing, curriculum learning, and SIGReg. Removing action conditioning degrades selected tasks; omitting the stabilization components causes training collapse or unstable latent dynamics. Temporal-bin resolutions of 3, 6, 9, and 12 hours are also compared.
legacy_cells.EL: Removing teacher forcing, curriculum learning, or SIGReg caused training collapse or unstable rollout behavior in the reported ablations.
legacy_cells.FL: A feedforward encoder maps each structured EHR observation to a 128-dimensional latent state. A neural predictor maps the current latent state and binary medication action to a state-dependent linear operator that propagates the prior latent increment. A shared linear decoder produces future continuous clinical measurements, and linear probes evaluate downstream outcomes. An MPC-referenced action-perturbation experiment compares simulated trajectories; no clinical execution loop is evaluated.
legacy_cells.FM: The authors introduce an action-conditioned latent dynamical model for structured EHR, using a state-dependent linearization predictor for incremental patient-state evolution. They evaluate latent trajectory fidelity, decoded clinical forecasting, downstream prediction, and sensitivity to changed medication-action sequences.
legacy_cells.FN: The paper reports 4.39M parameters for EHR-WM versus 141M and 143M for CLMBR and MOTOR. Forecasting is assessed across 79 continuous variables and 0–6, 6–12, 12–24, and 24–48-hour windows. Generated-versus-encoder latent discrimination is reported near AUROC 0.5; predictive performance varies by task.
legacy_cells.FO: The authors limit evaluation to MIMIC-IV, a single predominantly acute-care setting, and a restricted high-frequency feature set. The multiplicative transition may not produce action-driven displacement when the latent increment is near zero. Appropriate latent dimensionality remains unresolved.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors suggest external validation across institutions and longer-term populations, adding independent action-forcing terms or more flexible transition operators, and exploring adaptive, sparse, or hierarchical latent representations.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors distinguish their approach from autoregressive EHR models by explicitly parameterizing the evolution of a time-indexed latent patient state under clinical actions, rather than modeling evolution implicitly through event-token prediction.
legacy_cells.FR: The experiments demonstrate latent and decoded forecasting and action sensitivity under observational treatment sequences. They do not identify causal treatment effects, establish counterfactual validity, show clinical benefit, or provide prospective or external validation.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Pass the paper’s specified action and time context explicitly into the state-transition interface; preserve the boundary between predictive action sensitivity and identified intervention effects.
legacy_cells.FX: Complete 46-page extracted PDF text, pages 1–46, including title/abstract, introduction and related work, Methods §§3–3.1, main Results §§4–4.3, Discussion and limitations, Appendix dataset/task/architecture/training sections C–F, and extended-results sections G.1–G.9. Reviewed the text/captions for Tables 1–15 and Figures 1–23, including calibration and horizon results. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I are intentionally omitted from values and remain unchanged. Evidence is based on the complete local PDF text. Confidence is Medium because extracted table reading order is imperfect and Table 2 reports 29,871 test patients while Table 3 reports 29,971; the conflicting split count is not used. The action-sequence/MPC demonstration supports L2 action sensitivity only, not causal identification or clinical planning benefit. The supplied rubric refers to blueprint module IDs M1–M10 but does not define their mapping, so FS names the supported modules without IDs. Evidence QA: 61/92 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (66.3%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 77 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 15 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.
